accepted_semantics: Convert the requested claim and tolerances using the existing float conversion, then require finite values and finite nonnegative tolerances. Preserve numeric text and Boolean 0/1 inputs.

The selected result must be an existing numeric int/float/bool scalar; refuse rational/string/structured/null evidence, unknown fields, nonempty-string violations, and either missing member of the claim pair. With neither claim key, the ordinary response is unchanged.

Interpret the finite accepted binary64 actual, claim and tolerances as exact dyadic rational values; F(x) denotes the exact value of the accepted float. Do not compare against an unrounded physical value or dc_gain_exact.
Let E=abs(a-c) and L=max(A,R*max(abs(a),F(1e-12))). Use the original actual-value magnitude floor and max rule, with inclusive E<=L. Preserve the original float defaults 1e-4 and 1e-2 when omitted.
A truthful claim never changes an underlying passed=False to true. Keep existing specific evidence-only and undefined-result refusals.

evidence.exact: Canonical rational strings for E and L on every valid scalar comparison.
evidence.rendering: Round to a finite float when available, preserving nonzero subnormals. Nonzero zero-rounding gives null/below_float_range; overflow gives null/above_float_range. Zero has float0 and finite status.
evidence.refusal: Malformed or unsupported requests give passed=False and a reason without claim_check. An exact outside-tolerance verdict has complete claim_check and an accurate reason even if rounded E and L displays coincide.
evidence.json: Every unclaimed and claimed result must serialize with allow_nan=false. Preserve raw old decision observations if the old result fails serialization.

independent_oracle: Use signed integer units of powers of two from float.as_integer_ratio; align exponents for subtraction/comparison, multiply integer units for relative tolerance, and gcd-normalize for rational evidence. Do not use producer Fraction arithmetic in this receiver.
Independently prescribe each analytic within_tolerance result, and check the integer comparison agrees with it. All core transfers are a/(s+1).

Absolute boundary: exact 1+2^-54 exceeds1 although subtraction rounds onto1. Product boundary: (1+3d)(1+d)=1+4d+3d^2 for d=2^-27, while the exterior error is1+4d+4d^2. Overflow family reduces to comparison of2 with R. Floor family compares u with R*F(1e-12).
